name: José Almeida
action: He nods, folds the slip of paper into his pocket, and walks with Seu Olavo toward the nearby square. Once at the roda, José stands at the edge and asks Olavo, "No dues, no list, no one in charge, right?" then adds, "Today I’ll just listen—my voice and knee are worn out."
reason: José’s initial tendency was pulled in two directions: follow Olavo and possibly recite, or retreat alone, protect his depleted body, and keep the afternoon for planning, with an immediate impulse to delay by questioning the group’s informality. His reflective reappraisal softened that guarded delay. The memory of the spontaneous Mooca circle and his father’s saying about trusting one’s weight to the ground made the invitation feel more like informal community than institutional gatekeeping, while his trust in Olavo made a limited visit acceptable. But his hoarseness, aching knee, hunger, and unfinished notes kept him from full acceptance or performing. So he walks along and remains at the edge, asking about dues, lists, and leadership to test the roda’s informality, and states that he will only listen to protect his voice and knee. The main competing influence remains his suspicion of recurring groups, which is why he does not commit or join the center.
